summary: Founder of the S. D. Warren paper company of Westbrook, Maine, and father of a remarkable family; John's 6th cousin 6x removed.
bio:
Samuel Dennis Warren, known as S. D. Warren, was born on 13 September 1817 and founded the paper firm S. D. Warren & Co. of Boston, whose mills were at Westbrook, Maine. He descended from Lieutenant John Hammond through the Hastings family: Abigail Hastings, a second Abigail Hastings who married John Warren, Samuel Warren, born at Watertown in 1704, who married Tabitha Stone in 1728, Joseph Warren, born at Grafton in 1745 and died in 1808, who married Lois Lyons, and John Warren, born at Grafton in 1767 and died in 1828, whose second wife, married in 1804, was Susanna Grout. Through the Hammonds he is John's 6th cousin 6 times removed. His sister Anna Groat Warren was the mother of George Warren Hammond, who helped compile the Hammond family genealogy.

His children, all John's 7th cousins 5 times removed, made their own marks: Samuel D. Warren II (1852–1910) wrote The Right to Privacy of 1890 with Louis Brandeis; Henry Clarke Warren (1854–1899) was a Pali scholar and author of Buddhism in Translations; Edward Perry Warren (1860–1928) was the art collector who owned the Warren Cup and commissioned the Lewes version of Rodin's The Kiss; Fiske Warren was a single-tax utopian; and Cornelia Warren was a philanthropist. S. D. Warren died on 11 May 1888.

media.note: Samuel Dennis Warren (September 13, 1817 – May 11, 1888) was an American paper magnate and the founder of the S. D. Warren Paper Mill in Westbrook, Maine. Noted for his benevolence and paternalism, Warren built a commercial block adjacent to the mill, which is named in his honor.
